skill.name: httpclient-factory
skill.description: IHttpClientFactory and typed HTTP clients for .NET 10 applications. Covers named/typed/keyed clients, DelegatingHandlers, resilience with Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, and testing patterns. Load this skill when configuring HTTP clients, adding retry/circuit breaker policies, or when the user mentions "HttpClient", "IHttpClientFactory", "AddHttpClient", "typed client", "named client", "DelegatingHandler", "resilience", "retry", "circuit breaker", "hedging", "Polly", "AddStandardResilienceHandler", "socket exhaustion", or "Refit".
skill.summary: Configure factory-managed HTTP clients, resilience policies, request handlers, and mock-based tests for .NET 10 applications.
skill.author: codewithmukesh

security_audit.summary: All 44 static findings are false positives: 39 match Markdown backticks, and five match illustrative HTTPS addresses. The payment example enables default retries without disabling unsafe methods, creating a duplicate-charge risk. No evidence found of prompt injection, command execution, or intentional data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The payment client enables standard retries before sending a charge POST, without a local unsafe-method exclusion or idempotency protection.
remediation.suggestion: Disable retries for unsafe HTTP methods on the payment client, or require provider-supported idempotency keys before retrying charge requests.

3. **Resilience is not optional** — Every external HTTP call needs retry, circuit breaker, and timeo

semantic_findings.title: Payment Retries Can Duplicate Charges
semantic_findings.description: The payment client enables AddStandardResilienceHandler and sends a charge POST without unsafe-method exclusions or idempotency keys. Retrying an ambiguous failure could duplicate a charge. A later retry safeguard is not applied to this client.

content.value_statement: Poor HTTP client lifetimes and retry settings can cause connection failures or repeated operations. This skill guides .NET client registration, resilience configuration, request handlers, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Provides named and keyed HTTP client registration examples for .NET 10.
Explains standard resilience strategies and demonstrates retry and timeout customization.
Demonstrates bearer-token injection and correlation-header propagation through DelegatingHandlers.
Shows connection lifetime, idle timeout, decompression, and connection-limit configuration.
Provides an in-memory HttpMessageHandler example for isolated client tests.
Identifies common lifetime, shared-header, cancellation, and resilience-handler mistakes.
limitations: Contains guidance and C# snippets, not an executable library or an automated test suite.
Examples require project-specific types, service registrations, and compatible .NET packages.
Mentions Refit and hedging in a decision guide without complete implementation examples.
The payment example requires retry safeguards or provider-supported idempotency before production use.

output_examples.input: Which HTTP client registration should a new .NET 10 endpoint use?
output: Use a named client with keyed registration for direct endpoint injection.
Set the base address during registration and pass cancellation tokens for requests.
Configure one resilience pipeline and review retry safety for each operation.

output_examples.input: Review a payment client that uses standard resilience and posts charges.
output: Default retries can repeat a charge after an ambiguous failure.
Disable unsafe-method retries unless the payment provider supports reliable idempotency keys.
Test transient failures and verify that one logical payment cannot produce multiple charges.

output_examples.input: How can I test a service without calling its external API?
output: Construct an HttpClient with a custom HttpMessageHandler that returns controlled responses.
Inject that client into the service under test.
Check success and failure behavior without opening network connections.

best_practices: Use factory-managed clients and select dependency-injection lifetimes that preserve connection management.
Review retry safety before enabling resilience for payments or other state-changing requests.
Pass cancellation tokens, set authorization per request, and test clients with controlled handlers.
anti_patterns: Creating and disposing a new HttpClient for every production request.
Retrying non-idempotent operations without explicit safeguards against duplicate effects.
Stacking standard retry and hedging handlers without a deliberate pipeline design.

faq.question: Which .NET version does this skill target?
faq.answer: The examples target .NET 10, including keyed client registration and Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience.

faq.question: Does the skill install packages or run tests?
faq.answer: No. It contains documentation and examples. Your coding assistant must adapt them and run project checks separately.

faq.question: Does it explain named, typed, and keyed clients?
faq.answer: It demonstrates named and keyed clients. It discusses typed-client lifetime risks but does not provide a complete typed-client implementation.

faq.question: Are default retries safe for payments?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Disable unsafe-method retries or use provider-supported idempotency keys before retrying charge requests.

faq.question: Can the testing example avoid real network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The custom HttpMessageHandler returns an in-memory response instead of contacting the configured address.

faq.question: Can I use this guidance with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Generated changes still require project-specific review and testing.
